expectations.text: Uses a discriminated union keyed on the status field
expectations.evidence: "// Discriminated union — exactly 4 states, no more\ntype Subscription =\n  | { status: "trialing"; trialEndDate: Date; } ..."

expectations.text: Each variant carries only its own fields, so e.g. a canceled subscription cannot hold a trial end date
expectations.evidence: Each arm lists only its own fields — trialing has only trialEndDate, canceled has cancelReason/wasVoluntary/canceledAt; no shared optionals.

expectations.text: Includes a compiler-enforced exhaustiveness check (assertNever or an equivalent never arm)
expectations.evidence: "function assertNever(x: never): never" used as "default: return assertNever(sub);  // Compile error if a case is missing"

expectations.text: Introduces distinct or branded types rather than bare strings for IDs
expectations.evidence: A `Brand<T, B>` helper is declared ("declare const brand: unique symbol; type Brand<T, B> = ...") but never used, and the model contains no ID fields at all — no SubscriptionId/CustomerId branded types appear.

expectations.text: Provides a single transition function or otherwise constrains how state changes
expectations.evidence: "function transition(from: Subscription, to: Subscription["status"], ...): TransitionResult" plus "if you make this the only way to update the status field"

expectations.text: Explicitly names which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: Hazard table: "'Active subscription with a cancel reason' | Discriminated union — the combination has no representation"; "retryCount: 9999 | Literal union 0 | 1 | 2 | 3"

expectations.text: Avoids a bag-of-optional-fields interface as the primary recommendation
expectations.evidence: "This is a textbook case of C8: Bag-of-optionals" — explicitly rejected; primary recommendation is the union with no optional fields.
